subject: Critical Thinking
title: False Dilemma: Only Two Choices?
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: False Dilemma: Only Two Choices?.

hook.text: 'You're either with us or against us.' Really? There's no middle ground, no third option, no nuance at all?

buildup.text: False dilemma: presenting only two options when more exist.

discovery.text: Also called 'black-or-white thinking.' Real issues almost always have more than two possible positions.

twist.text: Politicians love this: 'Either we cut taxes or the economy collapses.' Both could be wrong. A third path could exist.

climax.text: The fix: whenever someone presents two options, ask 'What are options three, four, and five?'

punchline.text: Life isn't multiple choice with only two answers.

quiz.question: What is a false dilemma?
options: A difficult choice between two real options
Presenting only two options when more exist

details.summary: A false dilemma presents only two options when more exist, forcing a choice between extremes that ignores middle ground, third alternatives, and nuanced positions.
details.whyItMatters: False dilemmas are weaponized in politics and rhetoric to polarize debates and eliminate compromise. Recognizing them opens up the hidden alternatives.
takeaways: Most situations offer more than two options
False dilemmas force extreme binary choices
Asking 'what other options exist?' breaks the false binary

faq.question: What is a common example of a false dilemma in political debate?
faq.answer: You are either with us or you are against us. This eliminates neutrality, partial support, conditional agreement, and thoughtful disagreement, all of which are legitimate and common positions.

faq.question: How can you identify when a false dilemma is being presented?
faq.answer: Ask whether the two options actually exhaust all possibilities. Can you think of a third option? If so, the dilemma is false. Most real situations have a spectrum of responses, not just two polar extremes.
